title: Dominic and the Terminal
premise: Kestrel Eriksen smuggles forbidden memories between the two halves of humanity: the orbital elite of Halcyon and the frozen colonists of Terminus, whose cryosleep reactor is failing. When children on both worlds begin dreaming the same dream—a signal from the reactor's dying AI—Kestrel realizes the sleepers are waking early, and someone in power wants them never to wake at all. Hunted by customs, betrayed by her lover who serves Halcyon's council, she must choose which half of humanity gets the reactor's remaining power. In the end she sacrifices her own stored memories to bridge the two worlds, waking the children first and forcing both sides to share one future.
about_author: Casper Kavanagh is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard cargo vessels before turning to fiction, and his work is known for its salt-worn pragmatism and tenderness toward people who live between jurisdictions. He writes from a converted lightship off the coast of Maine.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. She runs a memory-chip shipment past Halcyon customs hidden in a hymn recording, establishing her rules: no names, no routes repeated, no attachments. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—the competence of a woman who has made invisibility an art.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Between worlds, she reviews her own black-market memories: her mother's face, a beach that no longer exists. We learn Terminus sleeps below while Halcyon hoards the orbit. Beat: grief worn smooth by repetition.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, a Terminus caretaker watching over sleeping colonists. The few awake children describe an identical dream: a counting voice, a red door. Ilsa sends a desperate message to the only smuggler who still runs the route. Beat: dread disguised as wonder.

chapters.title: A Job She Should Refuse
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Ilsa's message reaches her at a fueling station; the payment is impossible to refuse—passage rights and a name from her past. She takes the contract against every rule she owns. Beat: curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: Customs Officer Vane
chapters.summary: POV Vane, Halcyon customs, ambitious and watchful. He flags an anomaly in Kestrel's old manifests and begins building a case, less for justice than for promotion. Beat: cold institutional menace—power as paperwork.

chapters.title: The Red Door
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Docking at Terminus, she meets Ilsa and touches the dream herself via a child's recording: the reactor AI, DORMA, is broadcasting into sleepers' minds as it fails. Beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Sleepers Know
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The children's dreams contain fragments of engineering data—DORMA is asking for help the way it knows how. Ilsa realizes the countdown isn't maintenance; it's triage. Beat: maternal urgency meeting incomprehensible scale.

chapters.title: An Old Debt
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Her contact on Halcyon, council archivist Sef Oduya, reveals the council has known about the reactor for years—and voted to let Terminus sleep through its death. Beat: betrayal at civilizational scale.

chapters.title: The Man Who Waited
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. She reunites with Anselm, her former lover now a council security chief, and their old love reignites uneasily even as she hides her mission from him. Beat: love as both shelter and surveillance.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Vane seizes a memory shipment and finds DORMA fragments inside; he presents them to the council, positioning himself as the man who caught the conspiracy. Beat: ambition feeding on crisis.

chapters.title: Council of Half a Species
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. The council debates quietly letting the reactor fail—Terminus's power allocation would solve Halcyon's energy crisis for a century. Anselm abstains, hating himself. Beat: complicity dressed as prudence.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Branded a fugitive after Vane traces her, Kestrel flies the route with transponders dark, carrying DORMA's data core physically because nothing digital is safe. Beat: the smuggler finally smuggling something that matters.

chapters.title: The Price of Fuel
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. To pay a pirate toll she sells one of her own treasured memories—her mother's face—to a collector. Beat: the theme made flesh; survival always costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Anselm's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Ordered to hunt Kestrel, Anselm instead feeds her Vane's patrol schedules, crossing the line irreversibly. Beat: love against duty, duty losing—but not cleanly.

chapters.title: DORMA Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. With Kestrel's core installed, DORMA addresses the awake children directly: it can save half the sleepers, not all, and asks the humans to choose which. Beat: the impossible question arriving in a child's voice.

chapters.title: Vane Ascendant
chapters.summary: POV Vane. Vane uses the crisis to seize emergency powers, ordering Terminus's docking ring sealed and the route mined. Beat: corruption completing itself—power justified as protection.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Ring
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Kestrel, Ilsa, and the children make a run for the mining field in the Terminal, using smugglers' corridors only Kestrel knows. Beat: terror and exhilaration; her invisible life weaponized at last.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Cornered, Kestrel faces DORMA's choice: wake Halcyon's dissident families or Terminus's engineers, who alone can rebuild the reactor. She realizes the answer is neither—DORMA can split power if someone carries the decision into both worlds' networks. Beat: clarity bought at the edge of despair.

chapters.title: What Memory Is For
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. To carry DORMA's choice past firewalls, Kestrel must imprint the entire decision onto her own mind and walk it through customs personally—knowing Vane will strip her memories when caught. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Terminal Countdown
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. As the reactor hits critical window, Anselm turns on the council, arrests Vane mid-broadcast, and opens the ring—buying Kestrel ninety seconds. Beat: redemption too late to be clean, just late enough to matter.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. DORMA splits its final power: the children and engineers wake first, and Ilsa holds a waking child as ten thousand more pods flicker toward life. Beat: grief and joy inseparable—not everyone made it.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, One Sky
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Memory-stripped but alive, Kestrel wakes in Terminus infirmary knowing nothing of what she did; Ilsa gives her back a single chip—her mother's face, recovered. Below, Halcyon begins to descend. Beat: quiet hope; identity rebuilt from what others remember of you.
